newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PANTHERS SCORE THREE IN THIRD TO BEAT DEVILS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PANTHERS SCORE THREE IN THIRD TO BEAT DEVILS.

text.p: The Florida Panthers scored three goals in the third period for a 4-1 victory Sunday that ended the New Jersey Devils' 15-game home unbeaten streak, and it all started with an "own goal."

With the game tied 1-1, after a scramble in front of the Devils net, New Jersey winger Bobby Holik tried to clear the puck but accidentally swept it through the pads of goaltender Mike Dunham. Per Gustafsson was credited with the goal.
"The puck was bouncing, I tried to hit it hard but I was facing the net," Holik said. "It just happened. Of course I didn't mean to do it."
John Vanbiesbrouck, who finished with 31 saves, preserved the one-goal lead with a stellar blocker save on Bill Guerin following a 3-on-2 rush at 5:19.
"Crazier things happen the bigger the games get," Vanbiesbrouck said in reference to Gustafsson's goal.
Jody Hull gave the Panthers a two-goal cushion at 6:08 of the third period with his eighth of the season, redirecting Bill Lindsay's pass from the bottom of the right circle.

Steve Washburn added the final third-period goal. Dave Lowry tallied the first goal for Florida, which is 3-0-1 in its last four games. The Panthers halted an 0-3-3 road slide with their first victory away from home since January 23.
"It was a big confidence booster to beat the Devils ... in my eyes they're the the best team in the league," Panthers centre Tom Fitzgerald said.

"It was a real sound effort against a team that's really been on a roll and playing well," Florida coach Doug MacLean said. "It was a big win for us, but let's be honest, every game from mid-March is a big game. That was playoff hockey out there tonight."
The Devils suffered just their second loss in 11 games and missed a chance to take over sole possession of first place in the Eastern Conference.
Lyle Odelein scored for New Jersey, which had been 9-0-6 in its previous 15 games.
"Going 15 straight at home without losing, you're bound to be flat sometime," Devils defenceman Shawn Chambers said.
The teams have split four meetings this season (1-1-2).
In Buffalo, Donald Audette scored twice and Dominik Hasek recorded his league-leading 35th victory as the Sabres got their third straight win, 5-1 over the Boston Bruins.
Richard Smehlik and Derek Plante each had a goal and an assist and Brian Holzinger also tallied for Buffalo, 12-2-6 since January 29.
The Sabres, in first in the Northeast Division, moved within three points of Philadelphia and New Jersey for the top seed in the Eastern Conference.
Hasek allowed only Ray Bourque's power-play goal at 7:17 of the second period and finished with 27 saves. He moved one victory ahead of Colorado's Patrick Roy for the league lead.
The game was rescheduled from November 16 when the Jumbotron scoreboard at Marine Midland Arena fell to the ice before the game. The scoreboard will be replaced after the season.
In New York, Bruce Gardiner's goal with 2:13 to play snapped a tie and lifted the Ottawa Senators to a 4-3 victory over the Rangers, salvaging a split of a home-and-home series in the past four days.

Shaun Van Allen, Radek Bonk and Tom Chorske also scored for Ottawa, which avenged a 4-3 overtime home loss to the Rangers on Saturday. Ron Tugnutt made 38 saves for the Senators, who improved to 3-15 all-time against New York and 2-7 at Madison Square Garden.
The win pulled Ottawa within four points of the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference. The Senators moved into 11th place in the East, one point behind Tampa Bay.
Pat Flatley, Adam Graves and Wayne Gretzky scored for New York, which had a three-game winning streak snapped.

In Phoenix, Jeff Finley's first goal in almost four months at 6:31 of the third period snapped a tie and Nikolai Khabibulin made 35 saves as the Coyotes edged the St Louis Blues 3-2 in a key Western Conference battle.
Keith Tkachuk and Jeremy Roenick tallied in the first period for Phoenix, which improved to 5-1-1 in its last seven games.
The Coyotes, who had been 0-3-1 in their previous four home contests, moved into a fourth-place tie with Edmonton, two points ahead of St Louis and Anaheim.
Brett Hull and Mike Peluso had goals for the Blues, who had a three-game unbeaten streak ended.
